We are at the frontrunners of the digital transformation in healthcare. As a leading provider of advanced software, we are dedicated to a visionary mission: "No one should suffer or die because medical information is missing". Our goal is to develop groundbreaking solutions that make a quantitative difference in healthcare delivery - and for that, we are looking for the best of the best!

Your Contribution:

- You will be the driving force behind the development of a groundbreaking cloud strategy that elevates efficiency and flexibility to an unparalleled level. You will identify untapped potential for migrations and implement them with strategic foresight.
- You will manage high-calibre relationships with leading cloud service providers worldwide and ensure that their services meet our high standards. Your negotiation skills will be crucial here.
- You will oversee projects with your attention to detail to guarantee budget-secure and on-time implementations.
- You will conduct inspiring training sessions and workshops that elevate team members to the next level of cloud excellence and foster a culture of innovation.
- You are not only informed about current trends in the cloud industry but also work proactively to anticipate future developments and adjust our strategies accordingly.

What you bring:

- A completed university degree from a renowned institution in the fields of computer science, IT, or a related discipline with a special focus on cloud architectures.
- Proven, multi-year experience in developing and implementing advanced cloud strategies, ideally in a dynamic, globally operating environment.
- Deep expertise in cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), complemented by highly regarded certifications.
- Excellent communication skills in German and English to convincingly convey visionary concepts and inspire stakeholders at all levels.
- Exceptional project management skills paired with an outstanding analytical mindset and an unwavering drive for excellence.

What you can expect from us:

- Mobile Work: Work flexibly two days a week remotely and three days on-site.
- Attractive Locations: At our locations, you can expect fully equipped workplaces along with regular events like summer parties and Christmas celebrations.
- Development: Our in-house academy and our portfolio of external partners support your professional development.
- Health: Health is very important to us. In our in-house canteen, there is a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes, and in our fully equipped gym, we warmly welcome you to weekly classes.
- More is always possible: The kindergarten on our CGM campus in Koblenz helps our employees make their workday even more flexible. We also offer corporate benefits, the possibility of a job bike, pension schemes, and much more.

Diversity is part of CGM! We look forward to receiving your application regardless of disability, gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, and identity.

Convinced? Apply online now with your meaningful application documents (including your certificates, salary expectations, and the earliest possible starting date).

We are the leading provider of software in the healthcare sector. With our vision ‘No one should suffer or die just because some medical information is missing’, we want to create a culture that makes a sustainable contribution to the future of our healthcare system. Our work serves the goal of improving healthcare by ensuring that the necessary information is available anytime and anywhere. 

Your contribution:  

- In this role, you will conduct thorough assessments of IT systems to identify vulnerabilities and potential threats, enabling you to develop and implement robust risk management policies tailored to the specific needs of the organization. 
- You will collaborate closely with IT, cybersecurity, and business units to ensure that integrated risk management practices are in place and that all compliance with security policies and relevant regulations is maintained. 
- Additionally, you will lead incident response activities, effectively addressing and mitigating any breaches that may occur, while preparing detailed reports on risk management activities for presentation to senior management. 
- Building and fostering strong relationships with key stakeholders will be essential, as you provide expert guidance on IT risk management matters. 
- Lastly, you will stay informed about industry trends and emerging risks, ensuring that risk management strategies are continuously refined to align with the evolving landscape.

What you bring along:  

- Several years of experience in IT risk management or cybersecurity
- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field

- Very good German and English language skills
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, ability to convey complex information to non-technical stakeholders

- Feel Good Management: We offer you fresh food every day with a varied selection of dishes.
- Health: Use the gym and attend our free sports classes.
- Childcare: Our on-site kindergarten allows you to work more flexibly.
- Events: Take part in internal events and activities, these take place regularly on site but also remotely.

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that integrates basic, translational and clinical research to improve the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry (Director: Prof. Dr. Hadi Al-Hasani) investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying insulin resistance, skeletal muscle metabolism and type 2 diabetes.

For a new research project, we are looking for a talented and highly motivated

Doctoral Student (PhD / Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 65%)

to join our interdisciplinary research team investigating the molecular mechanisms by which repeated
cold exposure improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity.

Insulin resistance of skeletal muscle is a key feature in the development of type 2 diabetes, accounting for the majority of impaired postprandial glucose disposal. While lifestyle interventions such as exercise are well established, repeated cold exposure has recently emerged as a promising strategy to improve insulin sensitivity in humans, with reported improvements of up to 40%. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these beneficial metabolic adaptations remain largely unknown.

The project aims to identify the signaling pathways responsible for cold-induced improvements in skeletal muscle insulin action. A particular focus will be placed on testing the hypothesis that mild cold-induced muscle activation ("micro-shivering"), rather than brown adipose tissue activation, mediates these metabolic benefits.

The project combines translational human studies with mechanistic investigations in mouse models and offers extensive training in state-of-the-art metabolic and molecular research techniques.
Proteomic analysis of human skeletal muscle biopsies obtained from cold acclimation studies to identify molecular signatures associated with improved insulin sensitivity.
Mechanistic studies in wild-type and UCP1-deficient mice to investigate the effects of cold exposure and muscle activation on glucose uptake and insulin action.
Functional characterization of established and novel regulators of skeletal muscle metabolism, including AMPK, GLUT4, Rac1 and newly identified candidate proteins.
Investigation of GLUT4 trafficking and insulin signaling using advanced molecular and cellular approaches.

The project offers training in:

Mass spectrometry-based proteomics
Mouse models of insulin resistance and metabolic disease
Indirect calorimetry and metabolic phenotyping
Glucose uptake assays in isolated skeletal muscle
Molecular biology techniques (Western blotting, qPCR, gene expression analyses)
Immunohistochemistry and skeletal muscle fibre typing

In vivo electroporation and functional gene manipulation
Fluorescence-based analysis of GLUT4 translocation

You hold (or are close to obtaining) a Master's degree in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Molecular Medicine, Physiology, Biomedical Sciences or a related discipline.
You have practical experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques such as Western blotting, qPCR and cell culture.
Experience with metabolic phenotyping, skeletal muscle biology, mouse models or proteomics is advantageous but not required.
You enjoy interdisciplinary research and are interested in combining human physiology with mechanistic laboratory studies.
You are highly motivated, curious, and able to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment.
You have an excellent command of written and spoken English.

Your missionAs a Project Manager PV/BESS you will support the delivery of utility-scale Solar PV and BESS projects across Germany. The role will focus on owner-side project execution and EPC oversight from pre-NTP through construction, commissioning, COD, and handover to operations.

You will coordinate EPC contractors, technical advisors, site management, HSE consultants, grid stakeholders, and internal delivery teams to ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and to the expected technical and quality standards.

Projects will typically range from 20 MW to 100 MW and include PV+BESS hybrid systems with predominantly MV but also HV grid connection scope.

The role is remote/home-office based within Germany with regular travel to project sites as required.

Responsibilities

Project Delivery & Coordination
• Manage utility-scale PV and PV+BESS projects during pre-construction, construction, commissioning, COD, and operational handover phases.
• Coordinate owner-side project execution activities across internal and external stakeholders.
• Ensure project delivery in accordance with schedule, budget, quality, HSE, contractual, and lender expectations.
• Support transition from development to execution phase, including pre-NTP readiness activities.

EPC & Contractor Management

• Monitor contractor performance, schedule adherence, construction progress, and execution quality.
• Track contractual obligations, risks, variations, and claims in coordination with internal legal and management teams.

Technical & Advisor Coordination
• Coordinate external technical advisors, owner’s engineers, HSE consultants, commissioning specialists, and other technical stakeholders.
• Coordinate commissioning, performance testing, punch-list management, and COD activities.
• Support grid connection coordination together with external specialists and EPC contractors.

Construction & Site Coordination
• Coordinate site managers, HSE consultants, commissioning teams, and O&M stakeholders during execution.
• Conduct regular site visits during active construction and critical project phases.
• Monitor construction progress, interface management, quality issues, and project risks.

Commercial & Reporting Responsibilities
• Maintain project schedules, risk registers, action trackers, and reporting structures.
• Support budget monitoring and change-order tracking.
• Prepare project updates and reporting for senior management and internal stakeholders.

Operational Handover
• Coordinate project close-out, warranty management, defect resolution, and handover to asset management teams and investors.
• Support establishment of stable operational interfaces with O&M providers and operational stakeholders.

Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.
PhD student: Plant RNA Biology
The Wachter group at the Institute for Molecular Physiology (Faculty 10: Biology of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz) investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants. Our recent work identified a structured mRNA element that regulates specific DEAD-box helicase genes and revealed their critical role in controlling alternative splicing. Intriguingly, these functions appear to be linked to unique C-terminal features of the respective helicases. As a member of an interdisciplinary and international research team, you will investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the splicing-regulatory activity of these DEAD-box helicases, with a particular focus on the functional relevance of RGG motifs, subcellular localisation, and their potential involvement in phase separation. In collaboration with the Weinberg group (University Halle-Wittenberg), you will also explore how helicase targeting of pre-mRNA structural elements may intersect with the binding of splicing regulators to determine splice site choice. Your research will employ a multidisciplinary approach that integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, cell biology, and plant physiology, with Arabidopsis thaliana as the primary model system. You will benefit from extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure. The PhD project is funded by the DFG and can be integrated in the international PhD programme (IPP) in Mainz.
Applying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biology, including transcriptome-wide profiling of alternative splicing and mapping of protein-RNA interactions
Employing in vitro and in vivo experimental systems to address different levels of complexity and advance our understanding of the biological functions
Contributing to teaching activities for Bachelor’s and Master’s students within our group
Assisting with organizational and administrative tasks

Are you passionate about interdisciplinary research and eager to contribute to groundbreaking discoveries in the areas of biochemistry, structural biology, biophysics, cell biology, chemical biology and synthetic biology?

The International Max Planck Research School for Living Matter: from molecules to dynamics (IMPRS-LM) is a joint PhD program between the Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology, the TU Dortmund University, the Ruhr University of Bochum, and the University of Duisburg-Essen, located in the vibrant and multicultural Ruhr Metropolitan Area in Germany. The IMPRS-LM unites scientists from diverse disciplines to tackle a fundamental question in biology: How chemical components organize into the complex, dynamic systems we recognize as living cells? We welcome applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Biochemistry, Life Sciences, (Bio-)Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, or related fields.
